intent: a glass arthropod terrarium filmed as a 1990s science-classroom filmstrip, leaf insects swaying like dead leaves, condensation beads crawling down the glass, hand-lettered paper labels, frame-counter dot in the corner, a phonograph narration tone implied. Filmstrip only, no modern macro rig.

briefs.subject: A tabletop glass terrarium with an aluminum-framed mesh lid, framed straight-on like a single filmstrip frame. Inside: two leaf insects (Phyllium) — flat green-brown bodies with visible leaf-vein venation and legs shaped like broken leaf fragments — resting among a substrate of dead brown leaves, dry twigs, damp soil and a patch of moss. Condensation beads cling to the inner glass. Two hand-lettered paper labels are taped to the front pane (marker handwriting, lettering kept just soft enough to stay illegible — genus-style naming and a 'do not tap glass' note). A white frame-counter dot sits fixed in the top-right corner of frame, baked into the film print itself.
briefs.motion: All motion lives in the subject, never the camera. The leaf insects sway in slow irregular pendulums like dead leaves stirred by nothing: a two-second lateral rock, a pause, a faint flutter at the abdomen tip, one deliberate slow leg-step across a twig; antennae give tiny intermittent twitches. Condensation beads crawl down the glass in staccato gravity slides — a bead swells, elongates, snaps free, and leaves a cleared wet trail; two beads merge mid-descent; occasionally one drops from the mesh lid and ticks onto the leaf litter. A taped label corner lifts a millimetre in ventilation breeze. Everything else holds still.
briefs.camera: Locked-off frontal medium shot as if on a school AV tripod: 28mm-equivalent lens with modest barrel distortion at the frame edges, deep focus front-to-back (small-format classroom character, no shallow macro depth of field), terrarium centered with a hand's width of desk visible around it. Flat photoflood key from upper left putting a soft hotspot on the glass, its halation breathing fractionally with projector-lamp flicker; edge vignette and a faint yellowed frame border. Constant film gate weave: ±1–2px registration wobble with a slow vertical drift that re-settles every few seconds.
briefs.style: Aged 35mm educational filmstrip print: coarse clumped grain structure, dust specks and a stray hair in the gate, one fine vertical scratch, gentle emulsion flicker. Faded Eastman color drifted amber-magenta with washed blacks and milky highlights that halo; muted sap greens, dusty browns, yellowed paper tones. Low contrast, near-duotone classroom-print character; chroma bleed where the green insects meet glass highlights.
briefs.audio_direction: Implied phonograph narration: a warm mid-register voice-shaped murmur with a narrator's patient cadence that never resolves into intelligible words, pitched with slow wow-and-flutter wobble. Beneath it, a vinyl surface-crackle bed with occasional pops, a faint projector/fan hum, and low classroom room air. Sparse diegetic ticks: the plink of a condensation bead snapping free on glass, the dull tick of one landing on leaf litter, the dry rustle of insect legs over dead leaves; near-silence holds between events.
briefs.negatives: No soft dissolves or morphs, no tearing or warping of the glass geometry, no extra figures — no hands, faces, students or teacher entering frame — no modern macro rig feel (no shallow depth of field, no rack focus, no gimbal glide or slider moves), no sharp readable text (labels stay soft), no watermark or burn-in overlays, no glitch artifacts, no cartoonish insect behavior like hopping or flying.
briefs.identity_lock: Rectangular glass terrarium with mesh lid; two leaf insects with flat leaf-vein bodies and leaf-fragment legs; brown dead-leaf, twig and moss substrate; taped hand-lettered paper labels on the front pane with soft illegible lettering; condensation beads on the glass; white frame-counter dot fixed in the top-right corner; amber-magenta faded green-brown palette — all unchanged for the full duration of the shot.

qc.summary: The video features a high-quality, static shot of leaf insects in a terrarium. The subject is rendered with excellent detail and realistic textures. However, the temporal consistency is severely compromised by a major structural artifact: distinct vertical seam lines appear and disappear across the glass and background in several frames (e.g., at 0.00s, 5.00s, and 10.00s). Additionally, there is a distracting, bright circular flare artifact that flickers in and out of existence on the top right corner of the tank lid.
